note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing.
measured: 2026-08-06 at 0a2adb6 on the full tree, by `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline`.Re-stamped twice more during the validation pass, for findings the pass proved rather than argued. Note that `library/java/testing/src/main` classifies into the java.test bucket, which is why a fix to a main-source class lands there. Total code 159298. Programme total against the 167,711 starting line: -8,413, -5.02%. A note for whoever stamps this next: `--baseline` writes the measured value, so every bucket sits exactly on its limit after every stamp and there is never any headroom. That is the ratchet working -- a deliberate rise, stamped in the same commit, is the documented path -- but it does mean a one-line bug fix and its test cost a baseline edit, and the pressure that creates is what turns a ratchet into a rubber stamp. Read the reason field before assuming a rise was lazy.
